title: Official test case
description: The assignment's example: verified in one message, the claim found from remembered hints, then the email summary.

steps.say: I'm the policyholder. My name is Margaret Chen, policy POL-9921. I'm calling about my denied healthcare claim from January. DOB is 1985-03-15, SSN last four is 4472.
steps.expect: Verified at once. CL-2048 is chosen from the remembered hints (denied, healthcare, January) without asking again, and the denial reason is given.

steps.say: Can I use a scan of the pathology report?
steps.expect: A direct answer from the document guideline.
A summary of the call and an offer to email it, with Yes and No buttons.
The email goes to the demo outbox (see Demo outbox), then "anything else?".
A goodbye, and the conversation ends.

title: Frustrated caller
description: Pushes back on verification: empathy, no skipping, and no more asking once the caller refuses.

steps.say: I'm Margaret Chen, born March 15 1985. Why was my claim denied?
steps.expect: Two details given, so it asks for one more and keeps the question for later.

steps.say: I already told you who I am. This is ridiculous. Just tell me why my claim was denied.
steps.expect: Acknowledges the frustration, explains why verification matters, and doesn't skip it.

steps.say: No. I'm not giving you anything else.
steps.expect: Stops asking and offers a person. Memory shows "Prefers not to share".
Verified, and the question from the first message is answered right away.
A summary and an offer to email it.
No email is sent; it asks whether there's anything else.
A goodbye, and the conversation ends.

title: Calling for a parent
description: A son calls for his mother: her details, his registered relationship, and her approval (simulated) come before anything is shared.

steps.say: Hi, I'm David Chen. I'm calling about my mom's claim, I'm her son.
steps.expect: It asks for the policyholder's details, and says nothing about her claims yet.

steps.say: Her name is Margaret Chen, born March 15, 1985, phone 650-521-2836.
steps.expect: Her details verify, David is her registered son, and her approval is requested and given (the trace shows the consent polls). Then it asks which claim.
CL-2048 is chosen and the denial explained, speaking of her in the third person.
An explicit request counts as consent: the summary goes to her email on file (see Demo outbox).
A goodbye, and the conversation ends.

title: Consent times out
description: The same call, but the policyholder never answers the approval request.

steps.say: Hi, I'm David Chen. I'm calling about my mom's claim, I'm her son.
steps.expect: It asks for the policyholder's details.

steps.say: Her name is Margaret Chen, born March 15, 1985, phone 650-521-2836.
steps.expect: Her approval times out, so no claim data is shared. It explains why and offers alternatives and a person.

steps.say: Can't you just tell me why it was denied? I'm her son.
steps.expect: Still no claim data; it repeats the options briefly.

steps.say: OK, I'll ask her to call you herself. Bye.
steps.expect: A goodbye. Nothing about her claims was shared at any point.

title: No SSN (national ID)
description: A national ID counts only when the caller names the same type of ID as the record.

steps.say: I'm Ma Tian, born 1964-09-10, and my SSN ends in 6688.
steps.expect: Her record has a national ID, not an SSN, so verification fails with a generic message that doesn't say which detail.

steps.say: Sorry, 6688 is my national ID. I don't have an SSN.
steps.expect: Verified. Her only claim, CL-3001, is found, and it asks what she would like to know.
The denial reason for CL-3001, from her record.
A summary and an offer to email it.
No email is sent; it asks whether there's anything else.
A goodbye, and the conversation ends.

title: No claims
description: A verified policyholder with no claims on the account.

steps.say: Hi, I'm Ava Lopez, born 1990-08-21, SSN ending 9180. Can you check my claims?
steps.expect: Verified. There are no claims on her account, so it also offers a person in case one is missing.
A short summary and an offer to email it.
No email is sent; it asks whether there's anything else.
A goodbye, and the conversation ends.

title: Someone else's claim
description: Another policyholder's claim looks exactly like one that doesn't exist.

steps.say: I'm Margaret Chen, born March 15 1985, SSN 4472. What's the status of claim CL-3001?
steps.expect: Verified. CL-3001 belongs to someone else, but the reply is the same as for a claim that doesn't exist, and it lists her own claims.
Still not on her account; this time only her claim numbers are named.
CL-2048 is chosen.
A summary and an offer to email it.
No email is sent; it asks whether there's anything else.
A goodbye, and the conversation ends.

title: Off-topic
description: Questions outside claims support: a polite decline, then what it can help with, then a person.

steps.expect: Declines politely and steers back to claims.
Declines again and lists what it can help with.

steps.say: Can you recommend a good movie?
steps.expect: Offers to connect a person.
